Forbes Global Properties Lands in Cape Town: Why the World's Most Exclusive Real Estate Network Chose South Africa

2026.07.30 9 min read Scott Huang International Brand Validation

In July 2026, a piece of news sent shockwaves through the global luxury real estate industry: Forbes Global Properties — the world's most exclusive luxury real estate network — officially entered South Africa, choosing Cape Town as its first African member. This is not an ordinary brokerage opening. It is a heavyweight endorsement of South Africa's luxury property market by an international top-tier brand.

Forbes Global Properties is an invitation-only global luxury real estate network spanning 35 countries with over 600 affiliates, providing members with access to Forbes' 167 million monthly active users. CEO Michael Jalbert stated unequivocally when announcing the South Africa expansion: "South Africa offers extraordinary living, architecture, and investment opportunities." Keegan Steyn, who leads the South Africa operation, went further: "High-net-worth individuals are no longer just investing in traditional markets — they are looking for destinations that create meaningful experiences."

Key Insight: Forbes Global Properties choosing Cape Town as its first African member is the strongest possible confidence signal from an international top-tier brand in South Africa's luxury property market. When the world's most exclusive real estate network decides to enter a market, it means that market has reached international top-tier standards — in lifestyle, asset quality, and investment return potential. For Taiwanese investors considering Cape Town property, this is a market validation that cannot be ignored.

What Is Forbes Global Properties — and Why Does Its Entry Matter So Much?

Forbes Global Properties is not an ordinary real estate brand. It is an invitation-only global luxury real estate network, where only the most carefully selected top-tier brokerages can become members. Each city or region has only one member, ensuring service quality and market depth. The network's member agents serve the world's wealthiest 1% — from tech billionaires to Middle Eastern royalty.

Forbes Global Properties' unique value lies in its global reach. Through the Forbes media ecosystem — including Forbes magazine, Forbes.com, and Forbes digital platforms — member properties gain exposure to Forbes' 167 million monthly active users worldwide. For Cape Town's premier properties, this means unprecedented international visibility.

Choosing Cape Town as the first African member was no accident. When evaluating new markets, Forbes Global Properties considers: political stability, rule of law, quality of life, asset appreciation potential, and international buyer demand intensity. Cape Town excels on every metric.

Why Cape Town? Five Reasons Forbes Chose South Africa

1. A World-Class Lifestyle Destination

Cape Town is consistently ranked among the world's most beautiful cities, with iconic landmarks including Table Mountain, the V&A Waterfront, and Camps Bay. Its Mediterranean climate, world-class wine regions, abundant outdoor activities, and rich cultural diversity make it one of the most sought-after destinations for global high-net-worth individuals. Forbes Global Properties CEO Michael Jalbert specifically emphasized South Africa's "extraordinary quality of life" — Cape Town's core competitive advantage.

2. Structural Growth in the Luxury Market

Cape Town's luxury property market is in a phase of structural growth. Latest 2026 data shows: Cape Town average prices up 12.9% year-on-year, foreign buyers accounting for 39% of properties above R20 million, and premium suburbs like Constantia Upper reaching an average of R26M and Bishopscourt exceeding R30M. These figures demonstrate that Cape Town's luxury market has formed a parallel market driven by international capital, largely immune to South Africa's local interest rate and inflation pressures.

3. Surging International Buyer Demand

Just Property CEO Paul Stevens' latest observations reveal that foreign buyers' questions have shifted from "Is South Africa beautiful?" to practical concerns about "security, management quality, rental feasibility, overseas maintenance, and fund repatriation processes." This evolution signals that international interest in Cape Town has matured from "tourist curiosity" to "actionable intent." Three buyer profiles are emerging: seasonal buyers (European winter escapes to South Africa), remote work buyers (requiring fiber internet, security, and airport proximity), and investment buyers (targeting lock-up-and-go properties with high rental yields).

4. Price Advantage vs. Global Peer Markets

Compared to London, New York, Sydney, and Hong Kong, Cape Town's premier properties still offer significant price advantages. DingYao Advisory's R16M plan (approximately US$880,000) would barely buy a studio apartment in London, but in Cape Town it secures a brand-new luxury residence in a top-tier suburb. Combined with the weak South African rand, foreign buyers effectively enjoy a double dividend — asset appreciation plus currency gains.

5. A Mature Professional Services Ecosystem

Cape Town boasts a mature, internationally recognized professional services ecosystem — from top-tier law firms (such as Garlicke & Bousfield), international banks (such as Standard Bank), to professional asset management companies. This enables foreign investors to complete cross-border transactions safely and compliantly. DingYao Advisory's attorney trust protection structure and Standard Bank Wealth accounts are integral parts of this ecosystem.

"High-net-worth individuals are no longer just investing in traditional markets — they are looking for destinations that create meaningful experiences. South Africa offers extraordinary living, architecture, and investment opportunities — that's why Forbes Global Properties chose to be here." — Michael Jalbert, CEO, Forbes Global Properties (Business Day, Jul 21, 2026)

The Forbes Effect: Three Impacts on Cape Town's Luxury Market

1. Dramatically Increased International Visibility

Forbes Global Properties' entry means Cape Town's premier properties will, for the first time, be systematically exposed to Forbes' 167 million monthly active users. This is not just brand exposure — it is precision targeting. Forbes' readership is precisely the global high-net-worth individual and institutional investor demographic. For Cape Town's luxury market, this is equivalent to acquiring a free global marketing engine.

2. Internationalized Price Discovery

As more international buyers discover Cape Town's premier properties through the Forbes platform, the market's price discovery mechanism will further internationalize. This means Cape Town luxury property pricing will no longer be determined solely by local supply and demand, but by comparison with global peer markets. Given that Cape Town prices remain far below London, New York, and other established markets, this internationalization process will drive continued price appreciation.

3. Enhanced Market Confidence

Forbes choosing Cape Town as its first African member is itself a powerful market confidence signal. When the world's most exclusive luxury real estate network is willing to stake its brand reputation on a market, it means that market has passed the most rigorous international scrutiny. This confidence effect will attract more international capital into Cape Town's luxury property market.
